messages.author: 3d0e230fded30495
messages.subject: CAC and more questions
parts:
Hello,

Sorry, I'm writing again.

- I'm trying to generate shapes for CAC min and max (common allometry is confirmed). Is this the right way:

preds.CAC <- shape.predictor(CAC.plot$GM$fitted,
                             x= CAC.plot$CAC, Intercept = FALSE,
                             predmin = min(CAC.plot$CAC),
                             predmax = max(CAC.plot$CAC))  ?

- Since allometry is describing a small part of variation (~ 5%), I'm thinking of getting residuals from model procD.lm (shape ~ size + Species) and then generating PCA, maybe just to see the variation which is described by some unknown factor(s)... Is that a good idea? PCA of residuals from procD.lm (shape ~ size) model looks almost the same as PCA before removing the effect of size (which is expected).

- Also, in MorphoJ when you subset data, you always have to do Procrustes fit again. From reading in this group, I understood that's not advisable in the sense that data becomes incomparable?

Thank you for your time,

Ellen

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] CAC and more questions
parts:
Ellen,

 

Yes, your approach for CAC predictions is correct.

 

Since size explains little variation in your data, it is not a surprise that the two PCA plots are similar.

 

Correct. Performing separate GPA for each group is both unnecessary, and if one later wishes to compare among groups, makes the data incommensurate.


Dean
